Question: Before Ashley started a three-hour drive, her car’s odometer reading was \(29792,\) a palindrome. (A palindrome is a number that reads the same way from left to right as it does from right to left.) At her destination, the odometer reading was another palindrome. If Ashley never exceeded the speed limit of \(75\) miles per hour, which of the following was her greatest possible average speed?
Solution:
Since the drive lasts exactly three hours, maximizing average speed means maximizing distance. Ashley's speed never exceeds \(75\) miles per hour, so she travels at most
\[
3\cdot75=225\text{ miles}.
\]
Her ending odometer reading is therefore at most \(29792+225=30017\).

A five-digit palindrome is determined by its first three digits: its last two digits must repeat the first two in reverse order. Thus \(30003\) is a palindrome, and the next larger palindrome is \(30103\). Since
\[
30003\le30017<30103,
\]
the largest possible ending reading is \(30003\). This gives a distance of \(30003-29792=211\) miles and an average speed of
\[
\frac{211}{3}=70\tfrac{1}{3}\text{ miles per hour}.
\]
Driving constantly at this speed stays below the speed limit and attains that ending reading. The greatest possible average speed is therefore \(70\tfrac{1}{3}\) miles per hour, choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
